title: Who Guards the Benchmarks? Automated Auditing of LLM Agent Benchmarks
one_liner: 把任务说明、标答、评分程序和环境放在一起交叉检查，找出可能把合理解答判错的基准缺陷，再交给人复核。
classification_reason: 审计对象是任务说明、标答、评分器与环境之间的一致性，实证包括科学数据分析和生物信息学基准；审计本身不是执行科研任务，因此活动使用通用方法研究。

problem.text: 智能体被判错，可能是它没有完成任务，也可能是题目、标答或评分程序互相矛盾。作者关注后一类问题：执行型基准包含多个耦合的软件和文字材料，单独检查任何一份都容易漏掉错误。这里整理的是 2026 年 10 月的 v2 全文。

gap.text: 专家审核并不保证基准没有缺陷，尤其容易默认作者自己的分析选择已经写清。一般的答案评审也主要判断候选回答，没有系统检查题目自己的整套材料。BenchGuard 将这些材料合成一次审计上下文，而不是训练一个新的学习算法。

method.text: 每道题分别进行一次联合 LLM 调用，依次检查标答、评分逻辑、任务说明和环境，再合并同一修复即可消除的重复发现，拆开可独立修复的问题。静态检查并行补充明显配置错误；有智能体程序或执行摘要时可追加作诊断证据。输出含错误类别、严重程度、证据位置和建议修复，模型自评分不是校准后的正确概率，最终仍由人裁定。

trace.text: 一个任务要求每行输出药物的 SMILES，评分程序却查找药物名称；另一题让人计算差异表达，却在标答里悄悄加入性别协变量。审计器需要指出具体哪份说明与哪行代码不一致，而不是因为某种统计选择不同就宣布分析错误。附录还把非对齐发现区分为合理科学决策争议、环境惯例、澄清和真正可能改变答案的矛盾。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入是单题的指令、参考程序、测试与评分脚本、环境和数据说明，可另加执行轨迹。参考 Python 管线使用兼容 Harbor 的目录格式；Claude Code 和 Codex 的 skill 路径可直接在原生仓库发现这些材料。输出是供复核的结构化问题报告，不是对智能体能力的最终评分，也不是自动修改基准后的新版本。

results.text: ScienceAgentBench 的 102 题中发现了 12 个经原作者确认的问题，但这 12 个是审计后形成的发现集，不能当作独立的完整召回标答。BIXBench Verified-50 的 17 道专家修改题被拆成 24 个问题，五模型并集精确对齐 20/24（83.3%），含部分对齐为 23/24（95.8%）；最佳单模型 Opus 4.6 精确对齐 13/24。表3的全量五模型费用为 14.38 美元。这些是问题对齐结果，不是整体误报率或智能体正确率。

contributions.text: 论文把基准自身作为审计对象，提出覆盖标答、评价、指令和环境的四大类、十四小类问题，并提供有原文件证据的审计流程。它同时比较作者确认的发现、独立专家修订和不同模型的互补检出，强调“与已知问题对齐”和“发现确实为错”是不同判断。

limitations.text: 模型会把可接受的方法差异报成问题，也会漏掉领域约定；不与专家清单对齐的结果既可能是新发现，也可能是误报。附录 J.2 的五个强疑似 BIXBench 矛盾簇仍未获确认。ProgramBench 的扩展结果同样是初步发现。论文不覆盖所有开放交互任务，且没有通过审计分数证明科学分析的所有合理选择已被识别。

cost.text: 实现的主要成本是每题一次模型调用、可选的多模型并行，以及人工复核。正文设置最多 4,096 个输出 token；多数模型温度为 0，Gemini 使用 1 且只运行一次。14.38 美元只对应论文当时五模型审计 BIXBench 的 50 题，不能外推到任意模型、日期或更长材料。原文报告每个基准的完整非对齐结果人工分拣少于一小时。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：这直接研究科研智能体评测的可靠性，补充了 ScienceAgentBench 和 BixBench 的任务介绍。其价值是把可检查的材料矛盾交给复核，而不是用模型意见替代所有统计合理性判断；修复后的分数还可能向上或向下变化。

related.reason: ScienceAgentBench 是主要被审计对象之一；审计揭示了任务材料和程序评分之间的具体矛盾。

en.one_liner: Cross-checks instructions, reference solutions, evaluators and environments to surface benchmark defects for human review, including checks that reject valid alternatives.

sections.problem: An apparent agent failure may instead come from inconsistent instructions, references or evaluators. The paper audits such defects in execution-based benchmarks, where errors emerge across coupled textual and software artifacts. This card uses the October 2026 v2.
sections.gap: Expert review can miss assumptions inherited from the reference implementation. Ordinary answer judges also focus on candidate responses rather than the benchmark’s own artifact stack. BenchGuard builds a joint audit context; it is not a newly trained learning algorithm.
sections.method: One joint LLM call audits each task’s reference, evaluator, instruction and environment. It deduplicates findings resolved by one fix and separates independently repairable concerns. Deterministic checks supplement the audit; agent programs or execution summaries can be appended as diagnostic evidence. Outputs include category, severity, cited evidence and suggested repair. Model confidence is uncalibrated and findings require human adjudication.
sections.trace: One task requests SMILES strings while its evaluator searches for drug names; another reference introduces a sex covariate absent from the instruction. The auditor should identify a concrete cross-artifact mismatch, rather than treating every analytical difference as an error. The appendix separately triages defensible scientific choices, environment conventions, clarifications and answer-changing inconsistencies.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs are a task’s instruction, reference program, tests, evaluator and environment/data descriptions, optionally with execution traces. The reference Python pipeline uses a Harbor-compatible layout; Claude Code and Codex skill workflows can discover artifacts in native repositories. Outputs are structured findings for review, not final capability scores or an automatically repaired benchmark.
sections.results: On 102 ScienceAgentBench tasks, 12 discovered issues were confirmed by its authors; this post-audit discovery set is not an independent complete recall oracle. On BIXBench Verified-50, 17 expert revisions yield 24 atomic issues. The five-model union exactly aligns with 20/24 (83.3%) and partially or better with 23/24 (95.8%); Opus 4.6 alone exactly matches 13/24. The five-model audit costs $14.38. These are alignment metrics, not overall precision or agent accuracy.
sections.contributions: The work treats benchmark infrastructure as the audit target, supplies a four-category, fourteen-subcategory taxonomy and produces artifact-grounded findings. It compares author-confirmed discoveries, independent expert revisions and complementary model detections, distinguishing agreement with known issues from adjudication that a finding is genuinely a defect.
sections.limitations: Auditors may flag defensible methodological differences or miss domain conventions. Unaligned findings may be novel defects or false positives. Five strong BIXBench inconsistency clusters remain unconfirmed, and the ProgramBench extension is preliminary. Coverage is limited to the scoped benchmark types; auditing does not establish recognition of every valid scientific analysis.
sections.cost: Costs include one model call per task, optional ensembles and human review. The setup permits 4,096 output tokens, uses temperature 0 for most backends and temperature 1 with one run for Gemini. The $14.38 figure applies specifically to the reported five-model, 50-task BIXBench audit and is not a universal current price. Full triage of unaligned findings reportedly took under an hour per benchmark.
sections.relevance: Library analysis: This directly addresses scientific-agent evaluation reliability and complements ScienceAgentBench and BixBench. Its role is to surface inspectable artifact inconsistencies, rather than replace every judgment of statistical validity with model opinion; repairs can move scores upward or downward.
